inspection_summary: Verified the frozen hash and 1,130-line count, then inspected every line. The source develops an S-matrix/filling-fraction approximation for interacting quantum gases, uses boson-versus-fermion convergence to motivate a one-dimensional quasi-periodic fermion model for the critical strip, constructs its real-space potential, states the unproved pressure premise and approximation bottlenecks, and closes with a modular-channel interpretation of the zeta functional equation. Prose is coherent; several displayed formulas are text-layer fragile but recoverable from their checked surrounding prose.

sections_inspected.label: Front matter and abstract
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Identifies the finite-temperature Bose/Fermi scope and previews the quasi-periodic-potential RH proposal.

sections_inspected.label: I. Introduction
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Motivates the S-matrix thermal formalism, contrasts physics approaches to RH, and states the pressure-based heuristic.

sections_inspected.label: II.A. Free energy as a filling-fraction functional
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Builds the Legendre/stationary functional, entropy representation, pseudo-energy, and interacting free-energy equations.

sections_inspected.label: II.B. Two-body approximation
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Reduces interaction effects to a convolution kernel identified with forward two-body scattering.

sections_inspected.label: III. Second quantized Hamiltonians
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Relates a real-space two-body Hamiltonian to the lowest-order momentum-space kernel.

sections_inspected.label: IV. Hard core boson model revisited
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Derives the constant-kernel polylogarithmic thermodynamics and interprets the zeta pole through the absence of two-dimensional condensation.

sections_inspected.label: V. Fermi gases and the Fermi energy
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Uses the fermionic integral across the critical strip and separates interaction effects on pressure from the leading Fermi-energy relation.

sections_inspected.label: VI.A. Two-dimensional bosonic case
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Turns the saddle equation algebraic and packages pressure in Rogers dilogarithm, including rational special points.

sections_inspected.label: VI.B. Two-dimensional fermionic case
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Contrasts fermionic stability and analytic structure with the bosonic branch obstruction.

sections_inspected.label: VI.C. Many mixed particles
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Generalizes the algebraic system and pressure coefficient to coupled species of mixed statistics.

sections_inspected.label: VII.A. Quasi-periodic kernel in one dimension
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Posits the complex-power kernel, derives the low-temperature zeta condition, and isolates the pressure-modification premise.

sections_inspected.label: VII.B. Real-space potentials
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Constructs a log-quasi-periodic potential, derives its fermionic kernel, and identifies the convergence boundary.

sections_inspected.label: VIII. Conclusions and IX. Acknowledgments
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Records that the RH argument is not rigorous because the framework and leading-order control remain unproved; the remaining lines are non-mathematical.

sections_inspected.label: X. Appendix
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Equates finite-temperature and finite-size channels to motivate the completed-zeta functional equation.

sections_inspected.label: References and notes
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Bibliographic support and brief endnotes; no standalone derivation to segment.

accepted_units.title: Scattering data as the dynamical input to thermal occupation equations
accepted_units.why_material: It separates zero-temperature dynamics from statistical summation and explains why a self-consistent filling-fraction equation can reuse S-matrix data beyond exactly integrable systems.
accepted_units.context_note: Self-contained methodological motivation; its general method is instantiated by the functionals beginning at line 172.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose-dominant; only the partition-function display is formula-dependent and is legible in the normalized text.

accepted_units.title: From fermionic critical-strip convergence to a pressure-based RH heuristic
accepted_units.why_material: It states the paper's conceptual bridge: fermionic one-dimensional quasi-periodic interactions yield a zeta-controlled pressure correction, and RH would follow from the additional physical premise that nonzero interactions cannot leave pressure unchanged.
accepted_units.context_note: Carried v1 span already includes the zeta background, comparison with other physics programs, dimensional/statistical motivation, and the complete preview of the proposed implication.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equation (1) and the symbols for the critical strip and polylogarithm are needed; prose preserves the logical chain despite formula-layout risk.

accepted_units.title: Free energy as a stationary functional of filling fractions
accepted_units.why_material: The Legendre transform turns occupation numbers into dynamical variables and recovers physical free energy by stationarity, providing the representation on which all later kernel arguments act.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the definitions of free energy, pressure, density, the Legendre functional, and its saddle condition.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on equations (2)-(8); symbols are recoverable, though the calligraphic functional glyph is degraded in extraction.

accepted_units.title: Entropy functional and pseudo-energy deformation by interactions
accepted_units.why_material: It derives the free Bose/Fermi occupation law from energy minus entropy, adds an interaction potential, and rewrites stationarity as a pseudo-energy equation with a corrected free energy.
accepted_units.context_note: Starts with the free Fock-space setup and ends with the general interacting saddle/free-energy pair, so no external reconstruction is required.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-dependent, especially equations (10)-(19); surrounding prose fixes their roles, while the extracted functional symbol remains visually imperfect.

accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equations (20)-(24) are essential and legible enough to recover the convolution and saddle structure.

accepted_units.context_note: Contains the contrast with the bosonic integral and the fermionic saddle, density, and free-energy expressions.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Variational scattering-to-RH chain
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The paper's RH proposal is a composed representation chain from a stationary occupation functional, through a forward-scattering kernel, to a quasi-periodic real-space interaction whose leading thermal correction is zeta-controlled.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The composition remains conditional on the approximate two-body formalism, the low-temperature pseudo-energy ansatz, and an unproved pressure-response premise.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Particle statistics as the analytic-continuation gate
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Bosonic divergence at the zeta pole and fermionic alternating-integral convergence jointly explain why the proposed critical-strip realization uses fermions in one dimension and why the real-space transform imposes a separate half-plane boundary.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: These are source-internal analytic and physical motivations, not proof that the proposed Hamiltonian has exact thermodynamics or that boundary regularization exists.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Integral equations algebraize into dilogarithmic pressure systems
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Specializing the kernel and dimension compresses nonlinear integral thermodynamics into algebraic fugacity equations whose pressure is organized by Rogers-dilogarithm identities and extends compositionally to mixed species.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The rational examples are illustrative consequences of the constant-kernel approximation and do not independently support the RH argument.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Two physical representations of zeta structure
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Within the source, zeta appears both as a phase-space convergence/condensation boundary and as a modular consistency relation between thermal and finite-size channels.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The two appearances concern different physical systems and no source-grounded derivation identifies them as one mechanism.
